actions.reason: minbpe/base.py: replace_control_characters no longer uses str.translate with a dict-subclass mapping. That mapping takes CPython's per-character lookup path whenever the decoded token holds non-ASCII text (for example U+FFFD from partial UTF-8). The new version does three things. (1) It returns early when s.isprintable() is true: isprintable is false for every category C* and Z* character except space, so no escapes are needed. (2) Otherwise it classifies only the distinct characters, set(s), and caches the result. It then calls str.replace with the same \uXXXX escape for each control character found. The escapes are plain ASCII, so the order of the replacements cannot change the result. (3) Classification uses isprintable/isspace instead of importing the unicodedata extension. Every Cc character is below U+00A0, and above it the non-printable characters that isspace() accepts are exactly the Z* characters. load() also reads the model file as bytes and decodes it as UTF-8, applying the same universal-newline translation that text mode does; this avoids building a TextIOWrapper on each load. Outputs are byte-identical on the equivalence harness. In the sandbox, save_load_ir went from 467295534 to 441045577 (ratio 0.9438). The other metrics stayed within ±0.4%.

journal.text:
I changed replace_control_characters in minbpe/base.py. The old version used str.translate with a dict-subclass mapping. That mapping falls into CPython's per-character lookup when a decoded token holds non-ASCII text, such as U+FFFD from partial UTF-8. The new version returns early when s.isprintable() is true. I also edited the save path near lines 332-333.

The first three attempts were rejected. Their save_load_ir ratios were 0.9940, 0.9922 and 0.9916, and the required ratio is 0.9900. The fourth attempt was accepted in my sandbox at 0.9438, from 467295534 down to 441045577, with identical outputs. encode_ir rose to 1.0033 and decode_ir moved to 0.9980. All guards were within limits. The submitted candidate has 38 changed lines and is waiting on replays.

I now think save cost is dominated by escaping token strings, and that most tokens never need escaping. The small early versions did not help enough.

Next I want to check whether the encode_ir drift is noise. I also want to look at load parsing in base.py.
